questions.question: What is the output of the following Python code?
questions.code:
x = 10
y = 5
result = x + y
print(result)
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! x holds 10 and y holds 5. x + y computes 10 + 5 = 15, which is stored in result and printed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: x and y are integer variables holding 10 and 5. x + y computes 15.

questions.question: What is the output of this subtraction operation?
questions.code:
total = 100
discount = 35
payable = total - discount
print(payable)
questions.explanation_incorrect: total is 100 and discount is 35. 100 - 35 gives 65.

questions.question: Consider this tracing puzzle. What does this code print?
questions.code:
x = 10
y = 5
z = x + y
x = 20
print(z)
questions.explanation_correct: Spot on! Variable z stores the RESULT of x + y (15) computed at that specific moment. Changing x later does NOT recalculate z automatically!
questions.explanation_incorrect: In Python, variables store the calculated value at the moment the line runs. When z = x + y ran, x was 10, so z stores 15.

questions.question: How does Python evaluate: print(10 - 5 + 2)?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! + and - have equal precedence, so Python evaluates them sequentially from left to right: (10 - 5) + 2 = 5 + 2 = 7.
questions.explanation_incorrect: + and - are evaluated left to right in Python: (10 - 5) = 5, then 5 + 2 = 7.

questions.question: Why do we use brackets () in mathematical expressions in Python?
options: To force specific operations to evaluate first before other operators
Because Python requires brackets on all math lines
questions.correct_answer: To force specific operations to evaluate first before other operators
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Brackets have the highest precedence, allowing you to explicitly control calculation order.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Brackets () group operations so that Python calculates whatever is inside them first.

questions.question: What happens if you try to add an integer to a string variable: age = "25" and bonus = 5?
options: TypeError: Python cannot add a string (text) and an integer (number) directly
questions.correct_answer: TypeError: Python cannot add a string (text) and an integer (number) directly
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! In Python, types are strict. To do math, remove quotes from 25 or convert it to an integer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: "25" is a string (text) and 5 is an integer. Python raises a TypeError when trying to add them directly.
